code.originalText: Twenty-one-week review: weight, mood, the gastroenteritis, and care while travelling

text.paragraph: Twenty-one-week review: weight, mood, the gastroenteritis, and care while travelling. [S]

Empress Elisabeth returns five weeks after a gastroenteritis. The diarrhea settled within three days and she was back on her meal plan within the week, with no restriction afterwards. She did not have the blood test planned for two to three days after that visit, because she left to travel two days later and no laboratory was arranged. She has taken sertraline 50 mg daily. Her mood is better; she has had no thoughts of death. She walks about an hour a day and would like to return to some gymnastics. She leaves in a week to travel for six weeks, by sea and to her villa on the island, and asks how her care will continue while she is away. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1894-06-30; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Slim; weight 54.0 kg, BMI 18.3; temperature 36.5 C
Seated blood pressure 106/68, pulse 62; no orthostatic change; no edema
Brighter; reactive affect; no intent or plan to harm herself

Weight loss to a body mass index of 16.0 (47.4 kg at 172 cm), about 6 kg over six months, with fatigue, swelling of both ankles, dizziness on standing, slow pulse and cold intolerance; cause not established at intake; a restrictive eating disorder suspected, with thyroid disease, celiac disease, diabetes, malignancy and adrenal insufficiency to be excluded; eating disorders psychiatry consultation requested
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to her documented restrictive eating, low weight and swelling; superseded by the diagnosis at the consultation.

Anorexia nervosa, restricting type, moderate (DSM-5-TR), with compulsive exercise and frequent self-weighing, beginning in early adulthood; complicated at diagnosis by sinus bradycardia, orthostatic dizziness, ankle edema, mild anemia and leukopenia, low glucose, raised ALT and low phosphate after refeeding began
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the consultation, linked to her documented restrictive eating and exercise and to the retrospective diagnosis of anorexia nervosa (R).
Major depressive disorder, recurrent, moderate, with persistent grief for her son, who died five years ago; passive thoughts of death without intent or plan at intake
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis linked to her documented mourning and ever-deepening depressions; not a claim that she was so diagnosed.

Acute viral gastroenteritis, caught from a member of her travelling party, with mild dehydration, orthostatic hypotension and mild hypokalemia; no purging behavior; managed with oral rehydration and potassium; resolved
S — Synthetic acute problem; not a historical claim.

Low bone mass (osteopenia) of the lumbar spine and hip after decades of low weight: lumbar spine T-score -2.1, femoral neck T-score -1.8; FRAX 10-year probabilities 6.8% for a major osteoporotic fracture and 1.2% for hip fracture; no fractures
S — Synthetic modern finding on DXA; not a historical claim.

list.item:
Anorexia nervosa, restricting type, in weight restoration (F50.011). Weight 54.0 kg, BMI 18.3, up 6.6 kg since intake and recovered from the gastroenteritis. Pulse 62, no orthostatic change. Sodium 138, potassium 4.1 mmol/L, phosphate 3.6 mg/dL, magnesium 2.0 mg/dL. Not yet at a BMI of 18.5 and still afraid of weight gain, so treatment continues through the journey. [S]
Weekly CBT-E by secure video while she travels, with weighing at each session on a scale her companion keeps, not on her own scales.
Dietitian by video every two weeks; a written meal plan for travel and for meals at sea.
Blood tests once while away at a laboratory booked in advance, with results sent to the clinic.
Gentle stretching twice a week allowed; walks of up to 90 minutes a day; no long hikes or heavy gymnastics until the team agrees.
Return early, or go to a local hospital, for fainting, palpitations, rapid weight loss or vomiting.
A sealed travel letter with her diagnosis, medicines and the clinic's contact, kept by her companion.

Recurrent depression with persistent grief, responding (F33.1). PHQ-9 7, a 56 percent fall from 16: response. No thoughts of death. [S]
Continue sertraline 50 mg for at least a year after remission, with a full supply for the journey.
Safety plan updated with crisis numbers for each country she will visit; 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline and the clinic number confirmed.

Low bone mass (M85.80). 25-hydroxyvitamin D 34 ng/mL, now normal. [S]
Continue calcium and vitamin D 2,000 IU daily; repeat DXA in two years.
Second zoster vaccine dose given today.
